I'm requesting changes on one item before merge, plus a couple of should-fixes. The must-fix is verified against the live branch and is really yours to call, since you own both the code and the integration doc it touches.

Must Resolve Before Merge
1. The ?preview no-token path is a three-way mismatch between the two preview routes and the doc.
CodeRabbit flagged that .docs/integration/02-contentful.md still says ?preview Experience pages "fall back to Delivery API mode" with no token, and it's right that the code no longer does that. But the more important half is what the code does do now, which CodeRabbit didn't reach: in experience/index.tsx (L100–108), previewUnavailable short-circuits to an explicit "Preview is not enabled in this environment" message rendered at HTTP 200 with no <Seo noIndex/>. Its sibling /preview route handles the same no-token condition properly — res.status(404) + noindex (contentfulPreview/index.tsx L168–179). So the two preview entry points disagree, and on prod (where the CPA token is deliberately absent) /<real-slug>?preview becomes an indexable 200 — the missing half of the noindex gate from my #41 review. The doc compounds it: §9 (L128) even asserts "Both preview paths are noindex," which the code currently contradicts.

Fix: bring the previewUnavailable branch in line with /preview — add <Seo noIndex/> and a 404 via useServerContext() (the file already imports Seo; it doesn't yet import useServerContext, so that's the one addition) — then update the three doc references (the §3 diagram comment, the §4 CPA row, and the §9 bullet at L128) to describe the real behaviour: both paths fail explicitly, both noindex, no delivery fallback.

Should-Fix
Both pages duplicate the getContentfulConfig() → useMemo(createClient) block. Extract a single useContentfulClient hook — it's also the natural home for the token/host logic. (CodeRabbit has flagged this repeatedly.)
The new files don't pass npm run lint — ~100 Prettier errors (semicolons / brace-spacing). Run npm run lint:fix before merge.
(Optional) contentfulPreview/index.tsx L117 keeps locale in the getEntry effect's deps, but the effect only resolves the entry's content type, which is locale-independent — so a locale change triggers a redundant refetch + spinner flash on the /preview route. Harmless (the active guard covers the race) and editor-only; worth the one-token trim only since you're already in the file. Your call.

1.content:
PR #56 establishes one written standard for styling, `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, with a single source of truth for tokens (`foundation/` derives outward, never retyped) and one rule that matters most: a component's Chakra recipe in `theme/components/` is the only place its look is defined, which is why the `.zimm-btn-*` classes are gone and every button is now `<Button>` + `button.ts`.



Two things have flipped from what you may have been told: `var(--zimm-*)` now works in Storybook and is the convention inside theme files, and importing an already-overridden component by its `@salesforce/...` base path will silently render the unstyled base component in Storybook and Vitest while looking fine in the app.



Read the rules file before your next component, otherwise you'll build correctly against a convention we've just replaced, and the reason it'll pass your own review is exactly why it won't pass ours.

Claude Code is physically blocked from writing to develop or main via a branch-lock hook in the repo's .claude/settings.json.

Feature branches — day-to-day branch
When: every task, bug fix, or experiment.



git checkout develop
git pull origin develop
git checkout -b feature/SFCC-123_short-description
Naming format:feature/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}. Good: feature/SFCC-456_add-back-in-stock-button. Bad: feature/my-changes, feature/fix.

When done: open a PR targeting develop. qa.yml unit tests run automatically. One approval required before merge — develop is a shared integration point and your PR must not break it for anyone else.

Before every session:git branch --show-current (confirm branch) and git pull origin develop (merges happen frequently, even if you pulled this morning).

Hotfix branches — production emergencies only
When: a defect in production needs an immediate fix outside the sprint cycle.

Create from main — not develop:



git checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b hotfix/SFCC-999_critical-fix-description
Why from main not develop:develop has unreleased sprint work in progress. A hotfix branched from develop would accidentally include unreleased features. Branching from main keeps the fix clean and scoped to production state only.

Tier 1 rules still apply — even under deadline pressure, do not modify Tier 1 files without owner approval.

When done: PR into main. After merge, the fix must also be back-merged to develop to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint. (Merge commit vs. cherry-pick mechanism — confirm with the Integration Lead.)

Release branches — deployment targets, not working branches
When: a sprint is complete and a release is being promoted.

Release branches are created by squad leads or CI from a tagged develop state — developers do not create these. They exist as deployment targets for the SIT gate and cross-browser tests.

Pattern:release/v0.1.0, release/digital/v1.0.0.

What happens here: the full Digital SIT gate runs on every PR targeting release/**; BrowserStack cross-browser tests run on every PR targeting release/**; no new feature work goes here — only emergency release fixes after squad lead approval.

Making a code fix on a release branch
Do not edit the release branch directly for code changes. Branch off it instead so the CI gate runs against the fix before it lands.



# Step 1 — branch from the release branch, not develop
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git pull origin release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0_short-description
# Step 2 — make the fix
# Step 3 — PR back into the release branch (not develop)
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on SIT"
Once merged, squad leads apply the same fix to develop via a second PR to prevent the regression re-appearing next sprint.

When direct commits to a release branch are acceptable: only for changes with no logic — copy corrections, version number bumps, a boolean flag toggle. These require explicit squad lead approval before committing.

Claude Code on release/**: supervised mode — plan first, blast-radius check, confirm before every edit. Code logic changes must go through a fix/release-* sub-branch as described above.

develop — the integration branch
No direct commits. All changes arrive via PR from a feature/* branch. develop receives a deployment to Digital Dev and SIT on every push — a bad push breaks the integration environment for both squads simultaneously, which is why the PR review gate exists.

main — production state
No direct commits. All changes arrive via a release promotion or a hotfix/* PR. main always reflects the current production code. Tagging main with a semver tag (v0.1.0) is done by the release tooling at scripts/tagRelease.sh.

Tagging and versioning
Stage

Version format

Example

Pre-go-live sprints

v0.{sprint}.0

v0.1.0, v0.2.0

Go-live

Post-go-live patches

v1.0.{patch}

v1.0.1, v1.0.2

Post-go-live features

v1.{minor}.0

v1.1.0

Tags are created by running scripts/tagRelease.sh v{version} from main after the release PR is merged — this creates both v{version} and release/digital/v{version} tags.

Sprint boundary tags (sprint/{N}/{date}) are created automatically by CI when scripts/sprint.txt is updated. Update the file to the new sprint number when a sprint begins — increment it in a commit on develop.

As a Shopper, 

I want product cards to display relevant information for the surface I am browsing, 

so that each page feels appropriately tailored without inconsistent component implementations across the site.

Images for reference (Figma is leading):

image-20260727-234551.png
 

This story covers the build of a single shared Product Card component that supports multiple display variations via a style prop. Each variation controls which elements are shown — the component itself is built and maintained once. The component is scoped to the visual and interactive layer only — product data is sourced from SFCC. 

Variations in scope: 

Homepage

PLP

Wish List

Recently Viewed

Rollout Scope

AU
ME
EU - Domestic
EU - International

UK

Acceptance Criteria


Core component

Given a product is passed to the card component, when it renders, then the primary product image is always displayed regardless of variation.

Given the component is built as a PWA component, when imported into any page surface, then it renders correctly without page-specific logic embedded in the component itself.

PLP variation

Given the card renders on PLP, when it is in the default state, then the image, name, badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon are visible.

Given the card renders on PLP, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the size selector becomes visible and the price disappears and the tile image switches from the item/flat photo to the model photo.

Given the card renders on PLP, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear for the shopper to click through the product images.

Given the card renders on PLP, when on mobile, then the size selector is not displayed.

Given a product is out of stock, when the card renders, then the cart is greyed out and a notify me link appears on hover instead of price.

Home page variation

Given the card renders on home page, when it is in the default state, then the image and name are displayed.

Given the card renders on home page, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear for the shopper to click through the product images.

Given the card renders on home page, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the price (incl. was/now) appears.

Given the card renders on home page, when on mobile, then the user only sees the image and name.

Wishlist variation

Given the card renders on the wishlist, when it is in the default state, then the image, cart icon, name, colour, size, badge, and price (incl. was/now) are displayed.

Given the card renders on the wishlist, then there is a remove ('x') cta on the top right.

Given the card renders on wishlist, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the tile image switches from the item/flat photo to the model photo.

Given the card renders on wishlist, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear for the shopper to click through the product images.

Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)

Given the card renders on the View Full History Page, when it is in the default state, then the image, name, badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon are visible.

Given the card renders on View Full History Page, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the size selector becomes visible and the price disappears and the tile image switches from the item/flat photo to the model photo.

Given the card renders on View Full History Page, when on desktop and the user hovers, then the arrows appear for the shopper to click through the product images.

Given the card renders on View Full History Page, when on mobile, then the size selector is not displayed.

Given a product is out of stock, when the card renders, then the cart is greyed out and a notify me link appears on hover instead of price.

Variation extensibility

Given a new style is introduced in future (e.g. Search), when added to the component, then it can be configured without restructuring the base component.

STATUS UPDATE:
A draft PR is open covering this story together with SFCC-84 (Recently Viewed Full History), since they share almost all of their implementation.

WHAT’S SHIPPED: 
The Recently Viewed rail on PLP and PDP. Not on Cart, the user story names Cart as a surface, but neither the Cart designs nor the Cart Figma frames show the rail there, so we built to match the confirmed designs rather than the AC text.

WHY DRAFTED:
Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann storefront, so the rail currently runs on an interim, browser-only tracking mechanism instead (session storage for guests, local storage for signed-in shoppers). That means AC7 (history following a shopper across devices after login) isn't met yet, it can't be until Einstein is actually reachable. Swapping to Einstein is tracked as separate follow-up work once it's live.
